title: Attention micropacking and timebound prefill ramp for mixed-SKU fleets
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: In mixed-SKU fleets (H100 / L40S / A10) with MIG partitioning, prefill bursts often cause suboptimal kernel choices and KV cache churn. This increases tail latency and per-token cost for medium-length chat sessions. Current prefill logic ramps aggressively to maximize throughput, but when multiple tenants share MIG slices or when clocks are steered down during thermal events, aggressive prefill increases contention and triggers fallback kernels with poor latency.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Kickoff: scoped to two levers: (1) attention micropacking (grouping/tiling short sequences to better utilize attention kernels across token lengths) and (2) timebound prefill ramp (gradual microbatch ramp that respects MIG slice affinity and clock headroom).

2026-02-18 - Design review: PM and Infra agreed on telemetry hooks: per-request SKU tag, MIG-slice id, clock-state snapshot, kernel chosen, and prefill window length. Need lightweight schema change for runtime telemetry (runtime-telemetry-v2).

2026-02-25 - Trade-off discussion: Micropacking increases compute density but complicates latency SLO for single-user low-latency flows. Decided to make micropacking opt-in per route and default to disabled for P99-sensitive routes. Added a config flag: route.prefill.micropack.enabled.

2026-03-02 - Early prototype: implemented micropack scheduler that groups concurrently queued prefill requests by (model, quantization, SKU, sequence_bin). Observed 8-12% throughput improvement on A10 for batching of 2-4 short sequences, and 5-7% on H100 with L40S close behind. Kernel selector needed a hint to prefer attention-tiling kernels for micropacked inputs.
2026-03-08 - Telemetry spike: noticed KV cache eviction rate increase for mixed MIG setups when micropack size > 6. Added a guard to limit micropack size by MIG memory headroom snapshot.

2026-03-11 - Code review feedback from runtime team: rename scheduler interfaces to MicropackAdvisor and PrefillPacer; split clock-awareness logic into a separate module to keep kernel selection pure. Will follow up with a small refactor PR.
2026-03-12 - Performance dashboard link: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/runtime/perf/ENG-880777 (internal) — shows per-SKU perf delta and KV eviction histogram.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Micropacking enabled for selected canary routes shows >=5% mean latency reduction or >=7% per-token cost reduction on A10 without regressing P99 by more than 2% relative to baseline.
2) Timebound prefill ramp reduces KV cache eviction spikes by >=50% in mixed-MIG experiments versus aggressive prefill baseline.
3) Kernel selector accepts 'micropack' hint and prefers attention-tiling kernels when micropack is active; fallbacks behave deterministically and are logged.
4) Runtime telemetry exposes MIG slice id, clock snapshot, micropack size, chosen kernel, and prefill pacing decision for each prefill request.
5) Rollout config implemented: route.prefill.micropack.enabled (bool), route.prefill.pacer.window_ms (int), route.prefill.max_micropack (int), with safe defaults and canary gating.
6) No security or data-leakage regressions; passes internal security review checklist (networking and telemetry scrubbed).
implementation_notes: MicropackAdvisor: new interface that receives queued prefill candidates and returns groups keyed by (model_hash, quant, sku_bucket, seq_length_bin). Implemented in C++ runtime core with a thin Rust shim used by the scheduler on Dedicated nodes.

PrefillPacer: token/time-based pacer that enforces a ramp policy: initial microbatch size 1 for 0-10ms, then linear ramp to configured max over 250ms. Pacer consults ClockProbe API for current GPU clock headroom and MIG slice memory headroom before increasing micropack size.

Kernel hinting: extend kernel selection contract with a one-bit micropack_hint. When set, kernel-ranking boosts attention-tiling implementations if they are compatible with quant/seq shape. Add a fallback cost penalty if micropack_hint is ignored.
MIG/Clock awareness: sample clock and slice metrics at prefill admission time. Do not increase micropack size if (clock_state == throttled) or (slice_free_mem_pct < 20%).
Telemetry: add runtime-telemetry-v2 fields: micropack_size, pacer_phase_ms, sku_tag, mig_slice_id, clock_state, chosen_kernel, kv_eviction_delta. Log only IDs and aggregated counters to avoid PII.
Config: add safe defaults: route.prefill.micropack.enabled = false, route.prefill.pacer.window_ms = 250, route.prefill.max_micropack = 6. Canary enable on internal-preview cluster first.
Fallback policy: if prefill fails or latency regressions exceed threshold, automatically disable micropacking on that route and emit alert. Implement rollback automation in the rollout pipeline.
testing_plan: Unit tests for MicropackAdvisor grouping logic (edge bins, empty queue, single-item).
Integration test: end-to-end prefill flow with micropack enabled against synthetic workload (mix of short and medium sequences) on emulated SKUs. Verify chosen kernel events are emitted.

Canary experiments: run against dedicated canary nodes for each SKU (H100, L40S, A10) with and without MIG partitioning. Capture mean latency, P50/P95/P99, per-token cost, and KV eviction rate over 4-hour windows.
Fault injection: simulate clock throttling and low-memory on MIG slice to ensure PrefillPacer reduces micropack size and does not crash the scheduler.
Performance regression gates: require no P99 regression >2% and memory OOM rate unchanged. If gates fail, abort rollout and open follow-up ticket.
QA checklist: confirm telemetry fields appear in runtime-telemetry-v2, ensure dashboard queries populated, and safety toggle works in Console.
